input.old_string: MRG-GCN combines temporal representations with load-coupling, behavioral co-occurrence, and profile-similarity relations. The contribution is a controlled test of within-station relation gains and their interpretive scope, not a claim of novelty for the underlying graph convolution, gating, or temporal-network components. At Caltech, its overall MAE is 0.03890 kWh/15 min, 16.1% below a capacity-near TCN, but full AGCRN performs better and MRG-GCN does not lead on nonzero or event targets. At JPL, its overall MAE is 2.64%–3.36% below three preregistered baselines, while TCN has lower RMSE and lower nonzero- and event-target errors. Node-specific gates reduce overall MAE by 2.69% and 2.71% at Caltech and JPL, respectively; one shared-gate seed per site reaches the 60-epoch limit, so this result is budget-bound.
input.new_string: MRG-GCN combines temporal representations with load-coupling, behavioral co-occurrence, and profile-similarity relations. The contribution is a controlled test of within-station relation gains and their interpretive scope, not a claim of novelty for the underlying graph convolution, gating, or temporal-network components. At Caltech, its overall MAE is 0.03890 kWh/15 min, 16.1% below a capacity-near TCN, but full AGCRN performs better and MRG-GCN does not lead on nonzero or labeled-event targets. At JPL, its overall MAE is 2.64%–3.36% below three preregistered baselines, while TCN has lower RMSE and lower nonzero- and labeled-event-target errors. Node-specific gates reduce overall MAE by 2.69% and 2.71% relative to parameter-matched shared gates at Caltech and JPL, respectively; one shared-gate seed per site reaches the 60-epoch limit, so this result is budget-bound.
